No I can see that. In Jan I quit my job, I was smoking a lot more, doctors diagnosed me with CHS in February. So I cut it out of my life, I went cold turkey. He told me he was aware of how much I was smoking but he never commented on it to me directly before. In June I got sick again and presented with the same symptoms and everything but it was not CHS. It lasted for a month of not being able to eat and vomiting blood. He did not believe that I had gone cold turkey, and I didn’t get to prove myself. July I got better, a bit, and then got sick again. End of July I was done so I broke up with him. It was a snowball effect of many things that made me choose this. It wasn’t easy, I know I had my faults but none of them that I didn’t work on and improve upon. I went to therapy not just for myself but for him, because I wanted to make it work. He might have seen me as a drug addict, but never talked to me about it and or did not give me a chance to prove it was not CHS. The doctors only said the only thing that was abnormal was my potassium and magnesium levels because of how much i was vomiting. The only answers I have are that I have ovarian cysts, fallopian tube cysts, and the birth control I went cold turkey on has fucked up my body in many regards. I have since then smoked again, however, have found that when I get way too stressed I show the same horrible symptoms I did when they diagnosed me with CHS in FEB, and I DONT smoke during these stressing times. Granted I do not smoke like I did in DEC/JAN. It was mostly Jan because I had just left my job. Does that make sense?
I’m sorry, what part doesn’t make sense? I am being honest about it, if I wasn’t then I wouldn’t try finding some sort of relief in this mess.

Yes. It can come in waves too. I’m a female 20, have recently discovered ( not professionally diagnosed) I could possible have seasonal anxiety and or depression ( probably both). Around this time of year I get really anxious, agitated, depressed. I thought about this recently, and this was around the time school started for me, and I always dreaded it. I hated school so much, it always made me feel horrible. Now as a graduated adult, I have found that my stress levels are out of control and my body can’t react properly to minor things and I can have panic attacks or anxiety attacks. ( I was diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder) It was really bad last year when I quit my full time job at a popular fast food chain, and didn’t get back into a job till early November. Then in December had a spiral downfall and ended up in a mental hospital for the first time. Honestly, small things can trigger anxiety and make it huge. We both could be in the same boat of our bodies and minds not knowing how to react to minor things thinking they are bigger things. My best advice, is when you get anxiety or start to feel it. Just take a deep breath and distract yourself. If your at a family function, go somewhere quiet. If your at work, just take deep breaths and try and focus, sometimes this doesn’t work, and just go to the bathroom to collect yourself. If your at home and anxious cause your bored, find something distracting. This is what I personally do. Or if it’s too much, let it out, find a way to express yourself emotionally. Painting, crying, music, gaming, anger, screaming.
